1.Old Fort of Zanzibar
A coral-stone Omani fortress finished in 1701 on the ruins of a Portuguese chapel, its thick battlements enclosing an open-air amphitheatre, craft stalls and a small courtyard garden at the heart of the old harbor.

2.House of Wonders

2.Old Dispensary
Stone Town's most ornately decorated seafront building, completed in 1894 by wealthy merchant Sir Tharia Thopan as a charitable hospital, its carved wooden balconies and stained glass a showcase of Zanzibar's mixed Indian, Arab and European craftsmanship.

3.Hamamni Persian Baths
Public baths built between 1870 and 1888 for Sultan Barghash bin Said, their hot and cold rooms fed by underground aqueducts until the baths closed in 1920 — the only surviving example of Persian-style bath architecture in East Africa.

The decaying mansion of Hamad bin Muhammad, known as Tippu Tip, the island's most powerful 19th-century slave and ivory trader — its carved wooden door and black-and-white marble steps still visible from Suicide Alley, though the interior is now private flats.

From Hotel: 1h 10min → Kizimkazi
1.Kizimkazi
A fishing village at the island's southern tip pairing East Africa's oldest surviving mosque — its Kufic inscription dating construction to 1107 CE — with a boat trip to snorkel alongside the pods of wild bottlenose and humpback dolphins offshore.

2.Jambiani Beach
A white-sand southeast-coast beach where at low tide local women wade out to tend rope-strung seaweed farms rooted in the shallows, the crop dried and shipped abroad for use in food and cosmetics.

3.Paje Beach
A wide, shallow lagoon sheltered by an offshore reef, its steady side-shore wind and sandy bottom having made this stretch of the southeast coast Zanzibar's kitesurfing capital, with schools lining the beach for lessons or rentals.

A 12-table dining room built on a rock rising from the sea off Michamvi Pingwe beach, once a fisherman's lookout, reached on foot at low tide or by boat at high tide for a seafood-forward menu with an unobstructed ocean view.

Local Tastes
Zanzibar Pizza
A stuffed, pan-fried street-food dough parcel — minced meat, egg, cheese and vegetables folded into a thin sheet and griddled — unrelated to Italian pizza despite the name.
Forodhani Gardens food stalls · Shangani
Urojo · Zanzibar Mix
A tangy mango-and-turmeric soup loaded with potato fritters, boiled potato, cassava chips and hard-boiled egg, eaten as a late-afternoon street snack across the old town.
Forodhani Gardens food stalls · Shangani
Octopus curry
Grilled or coconut-braised octopus in a Swahili spice base of cloves, cardamom and cinnamon, a signature dish on nearly every Stone Town menu given the island's octopus fishery.
Lukmaan Restaurant · Stone Town
Kahawa · spiced coffee
Dark-roasted coffee brewed with cardamom or ginger, sold from brass pots by street vendors who signal with small cups clinked together — the everyday version of what Zanzibar Coffee House serves seated.
Mkunazini Road · Mkunazini

Getting Around
Bolt
Foreign number: accepted — Bolt's sign-up sends an SMS verification code to any country's mobile number, the same global flow used across its 45-country network.
Recently licensed for Zanzibar and reliable inside Stone Town, but coverage thins fast toward the beach areas — expect a boda-boda or tuk-tuk offer as often as a car, and longer waits outside town.
bolt.eu
Worth Knowing

A Muslim island first, a beach destination second

Zanzibar is over 95% Muslim, and Stone Town in particular expects modest dress — shoulders and knees covered for both genders — outside the beach resort areas; a light scarf or shirt over swimwear when walking back from the shore avoids the stares and occasional comments.

Public alcohol consumption outside a licensed bar or restaurant terrace is not customary and can draw unwanted attention, especially during Ramadan, when eating or drinking in public during daylight hours is best avoided even for non-fasting visitors.

The House of Wonders' partial collapse halted restoration inside, and no reopening date has been confirmed — it remains a facade-only stop, not a closed footnote to skip.

US dollar bills must be dated 2006 or later, unmarked and undamaged to be accepted at exchange counters and many hotels; older or torn notes are routinely refused, so carrying a mix of small Tanzanian shillings from an ATM avoids the problem entirely.

Reef-safe, oxybenzone-free sunscreen is worth packing before arrival — Mnemba Atoll is a marine-protected reserve, and standard sunscreen is genuinely harmful to the coral a snorkeling trip there is sold on seeing.
